name: Anju Agarwal
forbes_bio: Anju Agarwal is the widow of the late Rajendra Agarwal, who set up Macleods Pharmaceuticals with his two brothers in 1986 to make anti-TB medicines.
Rajendra Agarwal died in November 2025 at age 66.
Privately held Macleods Pharmaceuticals is among India's leading pharma firms. It produces generics for a range of diseases including asthma, osteoporosis and diabetes.
Her husband's older brothers, Girdharilal Bawri and Banwarilal Bawri, who are also billionaires, are chairman and joint managing director respectively.
forbes_facts: The company was named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks.
The families of Anju Agarwal and her two brothers-in law live in the same building in Mumbai.

name: Sandro Veronesi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Sandro Veronesi is the president of Oniverse (formerly Calzedonia), a hosiery and lingerie retail chain he founded in 1986 in Verona, Italy.
He got his start in the business by working for the Italian king of hosiery, Nerino Grassi, at the Golden Lady Company.
Today, his Oniverse group with subsidiary brands Intimissimi, Tezenis, and Falconeri, boasts more than 5,600 stores in 57 countries.
Veronesi is passionate about wine, and opened Signorvino, a chain of wine shops, cafes and restaurants across Italy.
forbes_facts: Veronesi started Calzedonia as a side business, while he was still working at the Golden Lady Company.

name: Park Soon-jae
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Park Soon-jae is cofounder and CEO of South Korean biotechnology company Alteogen, which focuses on biosimilars and bio-betters.
Alteogen is known for its ALT-B4, an enzyme with technology that allows drugs to be administered subcutaneously instead of intravenously.
In 2024, Alteogen revealed Merck had agreed to a licensing deal to use ALT-B4 for the drug giant's cancer drug pembrolizumab. Alteogen shares soared 25% in a day following the announcement.
Park's wife, Chung Hye-shin, served as the company's chief strategy officer until 2023.
forbes_facts: Prior to cofounding Alteogen in 2008, Park worked at LG Life Sciences and Hanwha Petrochemical, and was a postdoctoral researcher at MIT.

name: Isabel dos Santos
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2013-2020); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
forbes_bio: Isabel dos Santos is the oldest daughter of Angola's longtime former president, Jose Eduardo dos Santos, who stepped down in fall 2017.
In 2013, Forbes found that while Isabel's father was president, she ended up with stakes in Angolan companies including banks and a telecom firm.
In January 2020, Angolan authorities provisionally charged Dos Santos with embezzlement and money laundering. She denied the charges.
She owns shares of Portuguese companies, including telecom firm Nos SGPS, but in January 2020 said she was selling stakes in 2 other firms.
A spokesperson for Isabel told Forbes that she "is an independent business woman and a private investor representing solely her own interests."
Her father made her head of Sonangol, Angola's state oil firm, in June 2016, but Angola's new president removed her from that role in November 2017.
forbes_facts: Isabel dos Santos is nicknamed "the princess" in Angola.
Santos' mother, Tatiana Kukanova, met her father while he was a student in Azerbaijan. The couple later divorced.

name: Eric Hémar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Eric Hémar founded ID Logistics, a France-based international logistics and transport company. He still runs the company as chairman and CEO.
He launched the company in 2001 and took it public in 2012 on the NYSE Euronext in Paris.
Today, ID Logistics has a presence in 19 countries and generated $3.6 billion of revenue in 2024.
Hémar owns over 50% of the company's stock.
He's also served as president of the TLF Union, which represents French transport and logistics professionals, since 2019.
forbes_facts: Hémar started his career in the French government, first at its supreme audit court and then its transport ministry.

name: Stephen Winn
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Stephen Winn founded retail management software firm RealPage in 1998.
Its products help landlords manage finances and compliance requirements, and enable tenants to pay rent and file maintenance requests electronically.
An electrical engineer by training, Winn started his career working for his father's accounting software firm, Computer Language Research.
He eventually took over as CEO of the family business, and founded RealPage in 1998.
Winn took the Texas company public in 2010 and sold it to private equity firm Thoma Bravo in April 2021; he stepped down as CEO shortly after.
forbes_facts: RealPage's predecessor, Little Buddy, was a side venture of a tax software business Winn acquired to expand Computer Language Research.

name: Huang Zelan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2013); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Huang Zelan is the chairman of Chongyi Zhangyuan Tungsten, a mining concern.
His son Huang Shichun is a director of the company.
The company owns six mining rights and ten exploration licenses.

name: Jordi Rubiralta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Jordi Rubiralta derives his fortune from Werfen, a diagnostics company based in Madrid.
Founded by his late father Josep María Rubiralta and uncle Francisco in 1966, today the company covers diagnostics in hemostasis, acute care, transfusion, autoimmunity and transplants.
Rubiralta chaired the company until 2019 but remains on the board.
He led the expansion of Werfen in Germany and the U.S. with the acquisition of Tem and Accriva Diagnostics.
Rubiralta's family office, Yukon Capital, has carried out some of the most high-profile real estate transactions in Spain in recent years.

name: Lim Kaling
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Lim Kaling is an early investor and non-executive director of Razer, a gaming hardware maker that was set up in 2005.
The company has acquired a huge global following and sold millions of gaming laptops, mice, fitness bands and tablets. It went public in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529 million.
Lim and Razer cofounder Min-Liang Tan took the company private in 2022 in a deal that valued it at $3.2 billion.
Lim also runs the Lim Teck Lee group, a family business with interests in real estate, manufacturing and trading.

name: Ranga Raju Kanumuri
forbes_bio: Ranga Raju Kanumuri is the chairman of Hyderabad-based biopharma company Sai Life Sciences, which he founded in 1999.

Sai Life is a CRDMO or a contract research, development and manufacturing organization which does everything from drug discovery to research to manufacturing of drugs for larger pharma and biotech clients.
Son Krishna Kanumuri is managing director.
Sai Life debuted on the Indian bourses in December 2024 raising 30,426 million rupees.
Sai Life was founded as a chemistry partner to U.S. biotech outfits.
forbes_facts: He has a doctorate in pharmacy from the Massachusetts  College  of Pharmacy in Boston.

name: David Chen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025)
forbes_bio: David Chen is a cofounder of Singapore-headquartered online gaming and e-commerce firm Sea, best known for its hit mobile game, Free Fire.
He is the chief product officer of Shopee, the e-commerce unit of the NYSE-listed company. Previously he was Sea's chief operating officer and chief of staff.
Chen cofounded Sea in 2009 with Forrest Li and Gang Ye.
In 2023, Sea booked its first-ever annual net profit since its IPO in 2017.
Sea has rolled out digital banking services in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil.
forbes_facts: A computer engineer, Chen worked with Temasek-owned port operator PSA Corp before becoming an entrepreneur.

name: Gerald Engström
forbes_bio: Gerald Engström is a Swedish industrialist and co-founder of Systemair, a publicly traded manufacturer of ventilation systems.
He served as CEO of Systemair from 1974 to 2015 before becoming chairman until 2025.
Today Systemair operates in 51 countries with 90 companies and over 6,700 employees.
Engström owns a large portfolio of listed stocks, valued at over $1 billion.
forbes_facts: His daughter, Frida Engström, is CEO of fashion retailer Indiska, while his son, Niklas Engström, is CEO of RVM Systems, both companies in his portfolio.
